title: Fibre and image dimension bounds for finite-type schemes over a field
statement:
Let $k$ be a field, let $X$ and $Y$ be schemes of finite type over $k$ [def-weil-finite-type-morphism], and let $f:X\to Y$ be a $k$-morphism [def-weil-scheme-over-base]. All dimensions are topological Krull dimensions, with $\dim\varnothing=-\infty$ [def-kun-topological-krull-dimension]. Then
$$\dim\overline{f(X)}\leq\dim X.$$
Moreover, if $d,n\geq0$ are integers, $\dim Y\leq d$, and every scheme-theoretic fibre $X_y=X\times_Y\operatorname{Spec}\kappa(y)$ [def-pc-scheme-fibre] has dimension at most $n$, then
$$\dim X\leq d+n.$$
The closure in the first inequality is the topological closure in $Y$, and no dominance, properness, flatness, irreducibility or algebraic-closedness hypothesis is imposed.

source.place: Tag 0B2L, lemma-dimension-fibres-locally-algebraic, (2)(a) and its proof, applied to finitely many irreducible components; dim X - dim closure f(X) is the generic-fibre transcendence degree.

proof.text: If $X=\varnothing$, then $f(X)=\varnothing$, its closure and $X$ both have dimension $-\infty$, and both asserted inequalities are immediate. Assume henceforth that $X$ is nonempty. Since a field is Noetherian, the finite-type-over-Noetherian theorem [lem-weil-pbc-finite-type-over-noetherian] makes $X$ Noetherian, and [lem-sc-noetherian-finite-irreducible-components] gives finitely many irreducible components $X_1,\ldots,X_t$. Applying [lem-kun-dimension-finite-type] to $X$, to $Y$, and to each component shows that all global dimensions used below are finite.

source.place: Tag 0B2L, proof of (2), reduction to finitely many irreducible components; finite-type Noetherianity and finite-dimensionality

proof.text: For each component $X_i$, use [lem-weil-pbc-closed-subset-closed-subscheme] to give the closed subset its reduced closed-subscheme structure $j_i:X_i\hookrightarrow X$. The immersion finite-type clause (2) of [lem-weil-pbc-immersion-base-change-lft] and the finite closed-immersion statement [lem-weil-pbc-closed-immersion-finite], composed with the finite-type structure morphism of $X$ by [lem-sfb-finite-type-composition-base-change](1), show that $X_i$ is finite type over $k$. Let $f_i:X_i\to Y$ be the induced $k$-morphism and $Z_i=\overline{f_i(X_i)}$. Apply [lem-zl-irreducible-fibre-dimension-lower-bound] to $f_i$, writing $r_i=\dim X_i-\dim Z_i$. Its dense-open equality locus is nonempty because $X_i$ is nonempty; at a point of that locus, the local fibre dimension equals $r_i$ and is nonnegative by [def-kun-topological-dimension-at-point]. Thus $r_i\ge0$ and $\dim Z_i\le\dim X_i$ for every $i.$

source.place: Tag 0B2L, lemma-dimension-fibres-locally-algebraic, (2)(a), applied to each irreducible component

proof.text: The closure of the finite union $f(X)=\bigcup_i f(X_i)$ is the finite union $\overline{f(X)}=\bigcup_i Z_i$. Any irreducible closed subset of a finite union of closed subsets is contained in one member, so the Krull dimension of this union is at most the maximum of the dimensions of the $Z_i$. Combining this with Step 2 and the definition of the dimension of $X$ as the maximum of the dimensions of its finitely many irreducible components gives $\dim\overline{f(X)}\le\dim X$.

source.place: Tag 0B2L, proof of (2), finite-component reduction and the definition of dimension by irreducible chains

proof.text: Now assume $\dim Y\le d$ and every scheme-theoretic fibre $X_y$ has dimension at most $n$. For each $X_i$, choose its generic point $\eta_i$ and put $y_i=f(\eta_i)$. Apply the child node to $f_i:X_i\to Y$: it gives $r_i\le\dim_{\eta_i}((X_i)_{y_i})$. By [lem-pc-closed-imm-base-change], the fibre $(X_i)_{y_i}$ is a closed subscheme of $X_{y_i}$; under the homeomorphisms in [def-pc-scheme-fibre], its underlying space is the closed subspace $X_i\cap f^{-1}(y_i)$ of $X_{y_i}$. Local dimension is monotone for a closed subspace by the following elementary argument from [def-kun-topological-dimension-at-point]: choose an ambient open neighbourhood attaining the ambient local dimension; its intersection with the closed subspace is a neighbourhood in that subspace, and every chain of irreducible closed subsets of this intersection is a chain in the ambient neighbourhood. Thus the minimum defining the subspace local dimension is no larger than the ambient local dimension. This gives $\dim_{\eta_i}((X_i)_{y_i})\le\dim_{\eta_i}(X_{y_i})\le\dim X_{y_i}\le n$, where the last inequality is the fibre hypothesis. Since $Z_i$ is a closed subset of $Y$, $\dim Z_i\le\dim Y\le d$, and hence $\dim X_i=\dim Z_i+r_i\le d+n$. Taking the maximum over the finitely many components $X_i$ yields $\dim X\le d+n.$

source.place: Tag 0B2L, lemma-dimension-fibres-locally-algebraic, (2)(a), applied at each component generic point

lean.statement: theorem Scheme.Hom.finiteType_fibre_image_dimension_bounds {k : Type u} [Field k] {X Y : Scheme.{u}} [X.Over (Spec (.of k))] [Y.Over (Spec (.of k))] [LocallyOfFiniteType (X ↘ Spec (.of k))] [QuasiCompact (X ↘ Spec (.of k))] [LocallyOfFiniteType (Y ↘ Spec (.of k))] [QuasiCompact (Y ↘ Spec (.of k))] (f : X ⟶ Y) [f.IsOver (Spec (.of k))] : topologicalKrullDim (closure (Set.range f)) ≤ topologicalKrullDim X ∧ ∀ (d n : ℕ), topologicalKrullDim Y ≤ (d : WithBot ℕ∞) → (∀ y : Y, topologicalKrullDim (f.fiber y) ≤ (n : WithBot ℕ∞)) → topologicalKrullDim X ≤ ((d + n : ℕ) : WithBot ℕ∞)
